name: Plate Front Raise
description: The plate front raise uses a standard weight plate held with both hands at the edges (like steering a wheel), which places the forearms in a neutral position and distributes the load evenly between both anterior deltoids. The circular shape allows for a natural grip and encourages a consistent hand position throughout the movement. It is an accessible and practical anterior deltoid isolation exercise requiring minimal equipment beyond a single plate.

execution.starting_position: Stand upright. Hold a weight plate at the 3 o'clock and 9 o'clock positions with both hands. The plate hangs at thigh level in front of the body.
execution.setup_instructions: Begin with a 10 or 25 lb plate. The neutral-grip position reduces wrist stress compared to a pronated barbell hold.
steps: Step 1: Hold the plate at the sides, hanging at thigh level.
Step 2: Raise the plate directly in front of the body with arms nearly straight.
Step 5: Lower under full control to the starting position.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale on the raise, inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Using too heavy a plate and swinging the torso
Raising the plate above shoulder height unnecessarily
safety_considerations: Keep a firm grip on the plate at all times
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Thigh level to shoulder height (90 degrees of shoulder flexion).
coaching_cues: Like turning a steering wheel straight up
